model: Regulated utility dividend discount at cost of equity with exit multiple (engine route; rate-base compounding, net debt zero)

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-year CAGR (4.5%) is within 30% of EPS (4.9%) and 5-year revenue (5.0%), but 3-year revenue CAGR (1.2%) diverges -- fuel and purchased-power pass-through noise off a high FY2022 base, not an earnings signal. The larger gap is forward: the base path runs 7-7.5% per-share EPS growth through 2030 against a ~5% ten-year history, resting entirely on management's guidance and the data-center-driven capital plan.
historical_growth.notes: FY2020-FY2025 from the Metrics CSV: revenue 3,416 -> 4,362; diluted EPS 2.47 -> 3.14; common equity 5,888 -> 7,334. FCF CAGRs are undefined: reported FCF (identical to owner FCF less ~$20M SBC) is negative in every year of the window. Dividends per share grew ~6% a year (FY2023 $1.81 -> FY2026 $2.14).

scenario_narratives.base: Guidance delivered for 2027, then 7-7.5% per-share growth to 2030 -- slightly under management's 8%+ target to allow for dilution and financing cost -- fading to 3.5%. Dividend grows at the 60% payout floor and rises to 65% as the build matures. Exit at ~15.8x year-10 earnings.
scenario_narratives.bull: The uncontracted 2-4 GW data-center pipeline converts, the capital plan is raised again and EPS compounds 8.5-9% through 2030 with constructive Iowa and Wisconsin recovery; growth is still 4% in year 10.
scenario_narratives.bear: Large-load ramp slips or is resized, local opposition blocks new siting, the Iowa rate moratorium leaves cost and interest inflation unrecovered and equity is raised at lower prices; EPS growth falls back to 4.5-5% and then 3%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A regulated utility is a compounding equity base earning a regulator-set return; its owner cash flow is the dividend, and the retained earnings and new equity fund the rate-base growth that makes the dividend grow. The model therefore discounts dividends per share at a cost of equity and exits at a Gordon multiple well below today's P/E, rather than discounting a negative firm-level free cash flow. The 15% hurdle entry price will sit far below the market price: a low-risk 7-8% growth plus ~3% yield asset cannot deliver 15% without a large discount, which is a statement about the asset class, not a model error.
key_risks_to_valuation: Duration: roughly 70% of value is terminal; a 50bp move in the cost of equity moves value by ~12%
Data-center concentration: five executed agreements underpin the step-up from ~5% to 8% EPS growth
Dilution: ~25.6M forward shares outstanding plus up to $2.7B of equity 2027-2030; issuance below ~2x book would erode the per-share path
Regulatory: IPL base-rate moratorium through 2030 and earnings-sharing mechanisms cap realised ROE; WPL has no automatic fuel clause
Tax-credit monetisation ($285M sold in FY2025) is exposed to the OBBB Act phase-outs
FY2026 ongoing EPS is a guidance midpoint, not an actual; Q4 carries the reversal of a Q3 tax timing benefit

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular-session close); 52-week range 62.54-78.81
data_sources.financials: LNT_Metrics.csv (SEC XBRL, FY2008-Q1 2026); LNT_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt for the 2026-09-30 balance sheet, share count, forward sale agreements, convertible notes, dividends, capital plan and financing plan; LNT.duckdb kpis for rate base, authorized ROE and equity layers
data_sources.qualitative: LNT_Analysis.json (2026-11-15): FY2026 and FY2027 ongoing EPS guidance, long-term 8%+ growth target, $15.9B 2027-2030 capital plan, dividend targets, bull and bear cases

inputs.base_revenue_note: ENGINE MAPPING: the 'revenue' slot carries ONGOING EARNINGS TO COMMON for FY2026E = guidance midpoint $3.435 x 261.9M fully diluted shares = $899.6M. Guidance $3.41-$3.46, narrowed up on 2026-10-29 from $3.36-$3.46 (Analysis JSON guidance block). 9M-2026 GAAP diluted EPS $3.04 vs $2.59 (Q3-2026 10-Q :3669), ongoing $2.99; management says a Q3 income-tax timing benefit reverses in Q4. FY2025 GAAP diluted EPS $3.14.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted at the current price: 259.36M basic at 2026-09-30 (Q3-2026 10-Q :3723, :4214) + ~1.9M treasury-stock-method shares on the 18.67M-share 2025 ATM forward sale agreements (forward price $66.01, cash $1,232M; :4229-4237) + ~0.05M on the 6.91M-share 2026 ATM forwards (forward price $72.89, cash $504M; :4222-4224) + ~0.55M nonvested equity awards (:4628-4630). The $575M 3.25% convertible notes due 2028 are excluded: conversion conditions not met and zero shares in diluted EPS at 2026-09-30 (:4451-4459); the 2026 converts settled in March 2026 for $575M cash plus 834,811 shares (:4436). Held FLAT in the engine because growth_rates are PER-SHARE EPS growth -- management's 8%+ algorithm is per share and already nets the forward settlements (up to $650M in Q4-2026) and the up-to-$2.7B 2027-2030 equity programme (:5407). Per-share values do not depend on this count; only the headline equity total does.
inputs.net_debt_note: Held at ZERO by construction: the discounted stream (dividends) is post-interest, so debt is already serviced inside earnings; deducting it again would double-count (dcf-methods SKILL.md: never capitalise a post-interest flow and then subtract net debt). Debt and cash below are recorded for audit only.
inputs.total_debt_note: 2026-09-30: current maturities $374M + commercial paper $704M + other short-term borrowings $400M + long-term debt net $11,085M = $12,563M, tying to the 10-Q capitalisation table (Q3-2026 10-Q :3705-3713, :5466-5469). Debt/total capitalisation 62% (60% on the rating-agency junior-subordinated adjustment). Year-end 2025 was $12,028M.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2026E dividends to common = $2.14/share ($0.535 quarterly; $1.605 declared in 9M-2026, Q3-2026 10-Q :4286) x 261.9M = $560.5M. This is the FY0 flow the engine compounds. Reported FCF is NOT the stream (see reported_fcf).
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2025 reported FCF = OCF $1,169M - capex $2,483M = -$1,314M (Metrics CSV). 9M-2026: OCF $909M - construction and acquisition expenditures $1,806M = -$897M (Q3-2026 10-Q :3756-3760). Negative in 15 of the last 17 years and structurally negative through the capital plan ($2.86B 2026, $4.3B 2027, $4.7B 2028, $4.3B 2029, $2.6B 2030; :5529-5537); that capex enters rate base and earns an allowed 9.65-9.8% ROE, so an unlevered owner-FCF DCF would value the equity at roughly nothing -- a method artefact (AIA.NZ and the folder's utility builds), not a finding.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Metrics CSV StockBasedComp $22M; 9M-2026 compensation expense $29M vs $13M (Q3-2026 10-Q :4599, share-price-driven liability awards). ~0.5% of revenue and already EXPENSED inside GAAP and ongoing earnings (Alliant's ongoing EPS does not add it back), so sbc_pct_path is 0 and house = street; the band collapses.
inputs.buyback_note: No repurchases (kpis ShareRepurchases 0 for FY2023-FY2025). Alliant is a net ISSUER: 0.93M shares for $59M in 9M-2026 from forward settlements, ~25.6M shares / ~$1.74B of forwards outstanding, and up to $2.7B more planned 2027-2030. The dilution is netted inside the per-share growth path.
inputs.wacc_rationale: The 'wacc' slot is a COST OF EQUITY of 7.75%, because the stream is post-interest dividends. USD build: ~4.3% 10-year Treasury + ~0.65 regulated-utility beta x ~5% equity risk premium = ~7.5%, rounded up 25bp for above-sector leverage (62% debt/capitalisation, BBB+/Baa2 parent) and the dependence of the growth plan on a handful of hyperscale counterparties. Same rate as the folder's EVRG build and within the 7.5-8.0% used for other US regulated utilities. Identical across scenarios -- risk is charged once, in the scenario paths and weights.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable: leases are immaterial and all operating costs sit inside earnings.
inputs.nci_treatment: None: earnings are attributable to Alliant Energy common shareowners; subsidiary preferred stock was redeemed in prior years.
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE. Alliant Energy is a rate-regulated electric and gas utility holding company (IPL in Iowa, WPL in Wisconsin, plus a 16-20% ATC transmission stake): earnings = allowed ROE (IPL 9.65% base, WPL 9.8%) x the equity layer (51% / 54.5%) of rate base ($15.4B at FY2025), and growth comes from capex that regulators admit to rate base. dcf-methods/SKILL.md has no utility row; the operating-company row (owner-FCF DCF) is wrong here because reported FCF is structurally negative by design (FY2021-FY2025: -587 / -998 / -987 / -1,082 / -1,314; 9M-2026 -897) while the capex that drives it earns a regulated return above the cost of capital -- the firm-level DCF would be >100% terminal value against $12.6B of debt and return roughly zero or negative equity for a company earning ~11.5% on book. Per the skill's principle ('discount the flow the business actually produces, at the rate appropriate to whom it accrues') and the folder precedent for regulated utilities (EVRG, ES, AEP, EXC, D; GPT.AX/GMG.AX for the engine pattern), the model is a DIVIDEND DISCOUNT at cost of equity run through the engine: revenue slot = ongoing earnings to common; growth_rates = per-share ongoing EPS growth (nets planned equity issuance); ebitda_margin_path = dividend payout ratio, so engine FCF = dividends to common; sbc / D&A / capex / tax paths = 0 (all inside earnings); wc_capture 0; net_debt 0; terminal = min(Gordon on year-10 dividends at cost of equity, 28x year-10 dividends). Dividends, not earnings, are the stream because the ~35-40% retained (plus new equity) is what funds the growth already in the EPS path; capitalising earnings would count it twice. CROSS-CHECKS: (1) the base-case terminal Gordon multiple (1.035 / 0.0425 = 24.4x dividends at a 65% payout) implies a ~15.8x exit P/E on year-10 EPS against ~21x FY2026E today -- the valuation deliberately does not assume today's multiple persists; (2) a 65% terminal payout with 3.5% growth requires a ~10% ROE on retained equity, consistent with the authorized 9.65-9.8% plus ATC/AFUDC; (3) base FY2030 EPS of ~$4.55 sits ~3% below management's '8% annually' path ($4.67). FY0 is FY2026E (guidance midpoint), so Y1 = FY2027. Balance sheet, share count, dividends and capex plan are from the Q3-2026 10-Q text; the Metrics CSV ends at Q1 2026. The price is a regular-session close, not an after-hours print.

bear.narrative: One or more hyperscale agreements is delayed or resized (AI-capex pullback, local moratoria in Iowa and Wisconsin), capital is committed ahead of load, and the IPL base-rate moratorium through 2030 leaves cost inflation and higher refinancing rates unrecovered; equity is issued at lower prices and tax-credit monetisation shrinks under the OBBB phase-outs. EPS growth reverts to the pre-2025 4.5-5% run rate and then to 3%. The $2.25 dividend is still paid, so payout rises to the middle of the target range.

base.narrative: FY2027 EPS lands at the $3.68 guidance midpoint (+7.1%). 2028-2030 run 7.0-7.5%, a modest haircut to management's 'at least 8%' for financing drag (up to $2.7B of new equity and rising interest on 62% debt/capitalisation) and normal slippage in a $15.9B build, giving FY2030 EPS of ~$4.55. Growth fades to 3.5% by year 10 as the generation build rolls off. Payout: the $2.25 FY2027 dividend is 61.1%; the dividend then grows with earnings at the 60% floor of the 60-70% target range through 2031 and drifts up to 65% as growth capex and equity needs ease.

bull.narrative: FY2027 comes in at the top of the $3.63-$3.73 range and the 2-4 GW uncontracted data-center pipeline converts on top of the 3.4 GW already signed, so the capital plan is raised again and EPS compounds 8.5-9% through 2030 (FY2030 ~$4.80), with individual-customer-rate tariffs keeping recovery contemporaneous and DOE loan guarantees and tax-credit transfers holding down equity needs. Growth stays above 4% through year 10 on a larger rate base.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 28x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 20/55/25 rather than the house 15/50/35. Bear is lifted to 20% because the growth plan leans on five hyperscale contracts and continuous access to debt and equity markets at 62% debt/capitalisation; it is not pushed higher because near-term regulatory visibility is good (WPL rates set through 2027, IPL moratorium through 2030, 3.4 GW under executed agreements) and there is no solvency or covenant pressure. Base carries 55% because 2026 and 2027 are guided and the base path already sits below management's target. Bull is cut to 25% because it needs the uncontracted pipeline to convert, siting opposition to stay local and regulators to allow timely recovery -- several independent things at once.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
